strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets headless controllers resume local Runtime durable stores across a real schema upgrade boundary instead of relying only on a v1 admission gate.
Keeps schema compatibility, migration planning, interruption recovery, and partial-state refusal inside brownie-store before Runtime durable mutation.
Prevents tool, approval, replay, journey, checkpoint, and ledger evidence from being appended when the durable store is mid-migration or partially corrupted.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by replacing the prior v1-only schema gate with a concrete v1-to-v2 migration and interrupted-recovery path.
answers.new_capability: Runtime/store first-touch can migrate a v1 durable schema manifest to v2, write a bounded store-layout.json marker, resume after real process loss at each durable migration checkpoint, preserve existing v1 task/run/ledger/checkpoint artifacts, and fail closed on conflicting partial migration state before durable mutation.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-4 could initialize or adopt v1 manifests and reject future/corrupt manifests, but it had no vN-to-vN+1 migration planner, no in-progress crash marker, no idempotent interrupted migration resume, and no partial migration conflict detection.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A release build could claim durable schema migration readiness while only proving admission gating, leaving future local Runtime store upgrades dependent on untested best-effort behavior.
answers.non_duplicative: This is a corrective durable schema migration phase; it is not MCP approval recovery, protocol semantic contract work, module decomposition, platform/deadline hardening, CI workflow hardening, or owner license/publish work.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The behavior is internal to brownie-store and existing BrownieStore durable entrypoints; no JSON-RPC, CLI, or VSIX protocol surface is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The only new durable artifact is the bounded local store-layout.json marker and guard evidence, not a runtime report endpoint or diagnostic wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Existing v1 .brownie stores are migrated under the schema lock on first touch; interrupted migrations resume from durable markers after child process loss, existing task/run/ledger/checkpoint bytes are preserved until explicit post-migration mutation, and conflicting partial layouts fail closed before task/run/journey/checkpoint/ledger mutation.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous controllers can rely on Runtime refusing incompatible or partially migrated local state and converging interrupted v1-to-v2 migrations after process death without external scheduler authority.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the reopened P0 durable-schema-version-and-migration gap while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until RRP-7.1, RRP-5.1, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: brownie-store advances the current local durable store schema to v2 and declares an explicit DURABLE_SCHEMA_MIGRATIONS registry for the v1 to v2 migration path.

TaskStore::ensure_durable_schema writes migration_in_progress before migration work, resumes the same migration under the schema lock after real child process loss at each durable checkpoint, and only commits current v2 after store-layout.json validates.

The v1 fixture test preserves task identity, run ledger order, continuation/replay fingerprint material, and task state, ledger, and checkpoint bytes across migration before post-migration resume mutation.

Conflicting or malformed store-layout.json partial state fails closed before task mutation, while idempotent retry succeeds after either the in-progress marker or layout marker has already been written.

The phase keeps runtime_release_ready=false, does not change license/publish/release metadata or .github workflow files, and records RRP-7.1, RRP-5.1, and runtime-release-guard-ci as still required before release.

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or changes license/publish/release metadata
durable store schema stays at v1 with only an admission gate and no v1-to-v2 migration
migration lacks a registry/planner, durable in-progress marker, or idempotent interrupted resume path
partial migration state is silently overwritten instead of failing closed when conflicting
schema or layout manifests ledger raw prompt, provider response, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, or process output
CI workflow hardening, protocol semantic contracts, platform/deadline hardening, hosted scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or external adapters are added to this phase

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-4.1 changes guard-engine files, the current phase manifest, and Runtime release-readiness audit while closing the reopened durable schema migration gap. Review must confirm the v1-to-v2 migration is Runtime/store-owned, resumable after interruption, fail-closed for conflicting partial state, and does not hide RRP-7.1, RRP-5.1, CI, or owner release blockers.

exit_criteria: Current durable store schema advances to v2 with an explicit v1-to-v2 migration registry.
Migration writes a bounded migration_in_progress schema marker before v2 layout work.
Migration writes and validates a bounded store-layout.json marker before committing current v2.
Interrupted migration resumes idempotently after real process loss at the in-progress marker, layout marker, and current v2 manifest write.
Migration preserves existing v1 task/run/ledger/checkpoint artifacts and continuation/replay fingerprint material before explicit post-migration resume mutation.
Conflicting partial migration state fails closed before task mutation.

Rust durable schema tests cover migration behavior, process-loss interruption, v1 artifact preservation, partial conflict, and reopened blocker accounting; guard:durable-schema-migration detects deletion or drift of the required evidence.
Runtime Release Ready remains false; RRP-7.1, RRP-5.1, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner release decisions remain open.
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-store durable_schema -- --test-threads=1 covers v2 initialization, missing-manifest adoption, v1-to-v2 migration, real child process-loss migration resume at in-progress/layout/current-v2 checkpoints, v1 task/run/ledger/checkpoint fixture preservation, partial conflict rejection, malformed rejection, future-version rejection, and minimum-runtime-version rejection.

pnpm guard:durable-schema-migration validates source and audit presence for the migration registry, crash marker, layout marker, behavior test names, and reopened blocker accounting; this is drift/deletion evidence, not the primary behavior proof.

pnpm guard:durable-schema-migration:test covers negative drift for missing migration registry, missing interruption/process-loss evidence, missing v1 artifact preservation evidence, and hidden reopened blockers.

accepted_capability: Runtime/store can migrate v1 local durable schema manifests to current v2.
Interrupted durable schema migration resumes from bounded migration markers after real child process loss.
Existing v1 task/run/ledger/checkpoint data remains byte-preserved until explicit post-migration resume mutation.
Conflicting partial migration state is refused before durable mutation.
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-store durable_schema -- --test-threads=1 covers v2 initialization, v1-to-v2 migration, child process-loss resume, v1 durable artifact preservation, post-migration task lifecycle resume, and partial conflict rejection.
pnpm guard:durable-schema-migration and pnpm guard:durable-schema-migration:test validate durable migration evidence presence and negative drift cases.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime and brownie-store remain durable schema, replay, admission, ledger, checkpoint, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection layers and do not decide schema compatibility or migration authorization.

Schema and layout manifests are bounded compatibility metadata and do not persist raw prompt, provider response, file content, paths, secrets, environment values, executable content, or process output.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or OSS/public release posture.
Does not modify .github workflow files or bypass the workflow-scope CI blocker.

Does not add protocol semantic contracts, platform/deadline/failure-injection hardening, hosted scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing infrastructure, or external adapters.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected leaving the current schema at v1 because that would preserve only the admission gate and still lack migration proof.
Rejected silently repairing conflicting partial migration state because the release boundary requires fail-closed durable state handling.
Rejected ledgering raw path or content evidence because migration manifests must remain bounded compatibility metadata.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-4.1 closes the durable schema migration and interrupted recovery gap for local Runtime v1-to-v2 store upgrades.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until reopened Runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing Runtime durable entrypoints enforce schema migration internally.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-4.1.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-4.1.
